summary: James Trew reviews Teenage Engineering's EP-133 K.O. II sampler, a $299 device that looks cool and is far cheaper than the company's Field-series gear. He praises its intuitive layout, pressure-sensitive keys, good built-in mic and performative punch-in effects. He criticizes the lack of resampling, a song mode and the 12-voice limit, and notes early "fadergate" fader defects. He sees it as great for beginners and live play, and hopes firmware updates add features.
one_line: Engadget reviews Teenage Engineering's $299 EP-133 K.O. II sampler, praising its playful design and performance features while noting fader defects and missing resampling and song mode.
key_facts: The EP-133 K.O. II 64MB Sampler Composer from Teenage Engineering costs $299 and was revealed after a colorful website countdown.
Units reached buyers barely 24 hours after the K.O. II was revealed.
Early buyers reported defective faders, dubbed "fadergate"; one creator who took a unit apart found the internal pins were bent and not making a connection.
The K.O. II ships with the rotary and fader caps loose in the box, and the fader cap is unusually tight, leading to speculation that pushing it on damages internals.
The K.O. II runs on AAA batteries or USB power, is about 12 inches diagonally, and has a retro desk calculator look nodding to the Pocket Operator series.
Its "Super segment hybrid display" uses fixed custom icons, for example a red umbrella means undo.
The keys are pressure sensitive, and the built-in mic is surprisingly good; the sample manager tool works in a desktop browser or on Android via Web MIDI.
64MB of memory equals about 11 minutes of samples at 46kHz/16bit, halved for stereo; max sample length is 20 seconds, and presets use about half the memory.
The K.O. II has a 12-voice limit and only one master effect, and lacks resampling, which Trew calls possibly the biggest user complaint after fadergate.
There are four sample groups, each holding up to 99 patterns of up to 99 bars; scenes can be saved but can't be chained automatically, so there is no song mode.
There are 12 punch-in effects triggered by holding FX plus a black pad, and FX+7 adds the Level effect (rhythmic gating).

Firmware v1.1.1, the second official update, was released as Trew wrote; Teenage Engineering previously added the OP-1 Field vocoder synth over six months after release and the 1.2.38 OP-Z update almost three years in.
Trew considers it great for beginners and performative players but not as in-depth as Roland's SP 404 or Native Instruments' Maschine.
